issue_text: In AuditRun the outcome switch has `case env.IsError || env.Subtype == "error":` but no test exercises the `env.Subtype == "error"` disjunct on its own. Every RunFailed test fixture sets is_error:true (the only subtype:"error" fixture, `{"subtype":"error","is_error":true}` in TestAuditRunSeparatesTheThreeOutcomes, also sets is_error). A host that signals failure only via subtype (subtype:"error", is_error:false) would be misclassified as RunCompleted (or RunBlocked if a Stop hook fired), i.e. a failed session scored as clean — the exact fold-into-fine that RunOutcome exists to prevent.
why_real: Confirmed by mutation: deleting `|| env.Subtype == "error"` (leaving `case env.IsError:`) leaves the entire package test suite green. The disjunct is a real classification branch feeding a benchmark harness's outcome, and it is unpinned — a survivable mutant, not a style nit. Severity is low because AuditRun is not on the Stop-hook exit-code path (that is Emit/Build), and StopHookBlocks/Result still carry evidence in the struct.
tests_checked: blocked_test.go TestAuditRunSeparatesTheThreeOutcomes (all RunFailed cases set is_error:true; no subtype-only case), TestABlockedRunIsNotASuccess, TestCountStopHookBlocksReadsAnImperfectTranscript. Mutation `case env.IsError:` -> `go test ./internal/status/` PASS.
